issues.description: Conflict in the signature of messageOnRide between the exercise materials and the solution: The problem statement's UML and text (problem_statement.md) define Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. In the solution repository, Rideable is declared as String messageOnRide(int speed) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java) and Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(int speed). This parameter mismatch (no-arg vs. single int parameter) will cause student code that follows the problem statement/template to fail to compile against the provided solution, and it confuses which method students should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: change the solution's Rideable and its implementations (Pig, Seal) to a no-argument method signature `String messageOnRide()` and update their implementations to return the expected text "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" so they match the UML/problem statement and the template Main usage. Alternatively, if an int speed parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, UML, and the template Main to specify `messageOnRide(int speed)` and show example calls with a speed value.
